text:
**Answer:** 4 of our 5 NDCs depend on at least one single-source material in their active bill of materials. Together they account for **16,554 TRx in the last 13 weeks (weeks ending 2026-07-03 to 2026-09-25). That's 94.4% of our 17,540 TRx.** Only Oculon 5 mL has no single-source dependency.

| NDC | Product | Single-source material (only qualified supplier) | TRx, last 13 wks |
|---|---|---|---|
| 99101-0101-05 | Lacrivia 0.1% 5 mL | CMP-310 Emulsifier premix (S-201 Larchmont Contract Mfg, US); RM-221 Polysorbate 80 NF low-peroxide (S-104 Delmar Specialty Chemicals, India) | 7,017 |
| 99101-0101-10 | Lacrivia 0.1% 10 mL | same two | 3,425 |
| 99101-0202-05 | Cyclosporine OS 0.05% 5 mL | same two | 3,544 |
| 99101-0303-25 | Oculon 0.005% 2.5 mL | CMP-505 LDPE 2.5 mL dropper bottle (S-150 Quarry Hill Containers, Italy) | 2,568 |
| 99101-0303-50 | Oculon 0.005% 5 mL | none (every purchased material has 2 qualified suppliers) | 986 (not at risk) |
| **At risk** | | | **16,554 of 17,540 (94.4%)** |

**What drives the risk:**
- **The cyclosporine family is the biggest exposure: 13,986 TRx (80% of our volume).** Every cyclosporine product goes through the emulsion concentrate (SEMI-031), which needs the emulsifier premix (CMP-310). That premix has one qualified supplier, and one of its own ingredients (RM-221) also has one. So there are two single points of failure stacked on the same path. RM-221 has a second supplier on file (S-131 Pinecrest, China), but it isn't qualified, so I didn't count it as an alternate. Qualifying it would reduce the risk.
- **Oculon 2.5 mL (2,568 TRx) is exposed only through its bottle.** The 5 mL pack uses the 5 mL bottle (CMP-501), which has two suppliers. Moving volume to the 5 mL pack or qualifying a second 2.5 mL bottle supplier would help.
- **I excluded one old link.** Oculon's buffer concentrate (CMP-320) used RM-221 until 2025-06-30. That line has expired, so Oculon doesn't count as exposed to RM-221. An older, flattened BOM table (last synced 2024-11-30) could still show that link.

**Sources and definitions**
- **Supply data (Fabric):** `dbo.BOM`, exploded through all levels (5 is the deepest). I kept only BOM lines in effect on 2026-09-30. Materials came from `dbo.MATERIAL`, NDC links from `dbo.MATERIAL_NDC_XREF`, and suppliers from `dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL` plus `dbo.SUPPLIER`.
- **Single-source:** a purchased material with exactly one supplier marked as qualified (`QUALIFIED_FLG='Y'`). Unqualified suppliers don't count as a backup.
- **Commercial data (Snowflake):** "Our products" means `CORE.PRODUCT` rows with `CO_FLG='Y'` (5 NDCs). TRx is `SUM(TRX_QTY)` from `RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY` over the 13 most recent weeks, all channels.
- **Combining the two:** there's no cross-database join, so I matched the platforms by hand on the NDC, with dashes removed on the supply side.

**Assumptions and caveats**
- "TRx at risk" is the full recent TRx of any product with at least one single-source dependency. It's an exposure figure, not an estimate of the shortfall from a specific disruption. I didn't factor in inventory on hand or safety stock.
- Items made in-house (bulk, filled bottles and the pack kit) have no suppliers, so they aren't counted as single-source. Each is made at only one plant, though: PL-01 for cyclosporine, PL-02 for Oculon. That's a separate concentration risk.
- The other 55 finished-goods codes in the supply system (the FG-3xxx series) aren't in the commercial product master and have no TRx data, so they're out of scope.

FROM mats LEFT JOIN dbo.MATERIAL m ON m.MATERIAL_ID=mats.v LEFT JOIN dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL sm ON sm.MATERIAL_ID=mats.v LEFT JOIN dbo.SUPPLIER s ON s.SUPPLIER_ID=sm.SUPPLIER_ID
GROUP BY mats.v, m.MATERIAL_DESC, m.MATERIAL_TYP ORDER BY mats.v

SELECT * FROM dbo.BOM WHERE (PARENT_MATERIAL_ID LIKE 'FG-1%' OR PARENT_MATERIAL_ID LIKE 'FG-2%' OR PARENT_MATERIAL_ID LIKE 'FILL-%' OR PARENT_MATERIAL_ID LIKE 'KIT-%' OR PARENT_MATERIAL_ID LIKE 'SEMI-%' OR PARENT_MATERIAL_ID IN ('CMP-501','CMP-502','CMP-505','CMP-510','CMP-520','CMP-530','CMP-540','CMP-310','CMP-320')) ORDER BY 1,2
SELECT PROD_NDC11, COUNT(*) n, COUNT(DISTINCT WK_END_DT) wks, MIN(WK_END_DT) mn, MAX(WK_END_DT) mx, SUM(TRX_QTY) trx FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
SELECT WK_END_DT, DAYNAME(WK_END_DT) dn, COUNT(*) n, SUM(TRX_QTY) trx FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 16

SELECT pm.*, p.* FROM dbo.PLANT_MATERIAL pm LEFT JOIN dbo.PLANT p ON 1=0 WHERE pm.MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003','FG-2001','FG-2002','FILL-1001','FILL-1002','FILL-1003','FILL-2001','FILL-2002','SEMI-031','SEMI-044','SEMI-045','SEMI-060','KIT-100','CMP-310','CMP-505','RM-221')

WITH w AS (SELECT DISTINCT WK_END_DT FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY QUALIFY DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY WK_END_DT DESC) <= 13)
SELECT r.PROD_NDC11, p.BRAND_NM, p.PACK_DESC, COUNT(DISTINCT r.WK_END_DT) wks, SUM(r.TRX_QTY) trx_13w, SUM(r.NRX_QTY) nrx_13w
FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY r JOIN w USING (WK_END_DT) JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.PRODUCT p ON p.PROD_NDC11=r.PROD_NDC11
WHERE p.CO_FLG='Y' GROUP BY ROLLUP(r.PROD_NDC11, p.BRAND_NM, p.PACK_DESC) HAVING GROUPING(p.PACK_DESC)=0 OR GROUPING(r.PROD_NDC11)=1 ORDER BY 1
SELECT c.*, (SELECT SUM(TRX_QTY) FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY r WHERE r.CHNL_CD=c.CHNL_CD) trx FROM PHARMA_DEMO.REF.CHNL c
